audit.why: Rumble 48.13% over 561 games. Rumble owns levels 1-2, it evens at 3-5, and Kassadin takes 6 onward — the existing chart matches both the win rate and the scaling shape of the two champions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid text tells you to 'punish the 24-second cooldown' on Riftwalk.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds. There is no 24-second window to punish and a player waiting for one will simply never fight. What actually limits Riftwalk is its escalating mana cost on consecutive casts, and that is the resource to attack.
audit.corrected: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 falling to 2s; fight his mana, not his cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six separate lines credit Kassadin's PASSIVE with a magic shield that 'eats your first Q tick' and 'refreshes every six seconds'.
audit.why: Void Stone (P) is flat magic damage reduction plus unit-collision immunity — no shield, no refresh timer. The shield is on Null Sphere (Q), granted on cast, 9s at rank 1. The distinction matters enormously here: the reduction is permanent and applies to Rumble's entire all-magic kit every second of the game, which is a bigger problem than any shield.
audit.corrected: Void Stone = permanent magic damage reduction. Null Sphere = the shield, on cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly refers to a 'Q silence' and a 'W silence'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Null Sphere is damage, channel interruption and a shield — no silence. Nether Blade is an on-next-attack mana-restoring hit — no silence. And since Flamespitter is not a channel, Null Sphere does not stop it either, so the advice to rush both harpoons out before being silenced is built on an effect that does not exist.
audit.corrected: No silence in the matchup; keep casting through Null Sphere.

audit.why: Nether Blade is a 7-second auto-attack reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell that his short trade has started.

edits.before: Kassadin's passive shield blanks one Q hit but cannot absorb a full Danger-Zone Flamespitter channel — the sustained tick is the damage that gets through.
edits.after: Void Stone is flat magic damage reduction, not a shield — your whole kit is magic, so every tick lands pre-taxed. His real shield is on Null Sphere, magic-only too.

edits.before: Kassadin's Riftwalk lets him blink through your Flamespitter cone and onto you; his passive magic shield now eats your first Q hit for free every engage.
edits.after: Riftwalk blinks him through your cone and onto you every 5 seconds at rank 1, and a Null Sphere cast shields the opening burn — the lane turns here, permanently.

edits.after: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s maxed, so never wait it out — fight his mana instead, since blinks in quick succession cost steeply more

edits.after: Ride 50–100 Heat into Danger Zone Flamespitter — Void Stone taxes every magic tick, so only the empowered cone genuinely hurts him

edits.after: Null Sphere does not silence — it interrupts channels, and Flamespitter is not one — so keep casting; what it buys him is a shield on demand.

edits.after: Riftwalk blinks him through your cone every 5 seconds at rank 1 and Void Stone taxes all of your magic damage on the way in — the lane flips here for good.

edits.before: At level 1 Kassadin is legitimately weak — no Riftwalk, no blink, just a melee mage with a passive magic shield. Walk up and activate Flamespitter on every last-hit attempt he makes; even one hit forces him back. Level 2 you add Electro-Harpoon: double-cast the slow to keep him in Flamespitter range long enough to burn the whole channel into him. The catch is that his passive magic shield will eat one of those Q ticks for free, so you need the full Danger-Zone-empowered channel at 50–100 Heat — not a two-second clip — to actually threaten his HP bar. Level 3 brings your full kit but his Q silence means you need to fire both Electro-Harpoon casts BEFORE he can silence you, or he walks away and your second harpoon is lost.
edits.after: At level 1 Kassadin is legitimately weak — no Riftwalk, no blink, just a melee mage. Walk up and burn Flamespitter on every last-hit he goes for; even one pass forces him back. Level 2 you add Electro Harpoon: double-cast the slow to keep him inside the cone for its full three seconds. The catch is Void Stone, a permanent magic damage reduction rather than a shield, so a clipped cone does nothing — you need 50–100 Heat and the empowered version to move his HP bar at all. Level 3 he can answer with Null Sphere, which shields him and interrupts channels, but Flamespitter is not a channel and there is no silence in his kit: keep casting, and spend both harpoons on the slow rather than saving one.

edits.before: At level 6 everything shifts. Riftwalk lets Kassadin blink straight through your Flamespitter cone, bypassing the sustained damage entirely, and land right on top of you — exactly the scenario where Overheat silence or a mistimed W makes you defenseless. His magic shield now refreshes every six seconds off your own spells. Trade with the wave between you: keep it near your tower so his Riftwalk angle is narrower and your Scrap Shield has time to proc before he closes. Use Equalizer across river or to cut off his escape route after a gank, not as a pure 1v1 tool — it is your strongest weapon and its value is map-wide, not just in this lane. If he burns Riftwalk aggressively, punish the 24-second cooldown with one clean Danger-Zone trade, but do not commit your W into his Q silence.
edits.after: At level 6 everything shifts. Riftwalk blinks Kassadin straight through your Flamespitter cone and onto you, and at 5 seconds on rank 1 falling to 2 at rank 3 there is no cooldown to wait out — the only brake on it is mana, because consecutive blinks cost him steeply more. Null Sphere shields him on cast and Void Stone reduces magic damage permanently, so your entire kit arrives pre-taxed and only the empowered Danger Zone cone genuinely matters. Trade with the wave near your tower so his blink angle is narrow and Scrap Shield has time to proc before he lands. Use The Equalizer across the river or to cut his path after a gank, never as a pure 1v1 tool — its value is map-wide. His short-trade tell is Nether Blade, a 7-second auto reset: step out on the wind-up, not on the cast.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s: far too short to wait out — drain his mana, do not track a cooldown. - Null Sphere 9s is both his shield and the only real gap in his cover. - The Equalizer 130/105/80: kill windows only.

notes: Two calibration-grade errors here. First, the page told the player to 'punish the 24-second cooldown' on Riftwalk — it is 5/3.5/2 seconds, so that advice means never fighting. Second, six lines attributed a refreshing magic shield to Kassadin's passive; Void Stone is permanent magic damage REDUCTION plus collision immunity, and the shield belongs to Null Sphere on cast. The reduction is the more important fact anyway, because Rumble's entire kit is magic. Also removed a 'Q silence' and a 'W silence' that do not exist in his kit — Null Sphere interrupts channels, and Flamespitter is not a channel, so nothing in Kassadin's kit stops Rumble mid-cast. Nether Blade's 7-second auto reset added as the short-trade tell.
